items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because some of the examples in the AssetTagHelper and AssetUrlHelper API docs show output that the helpers don't produce.

  • preload_link_tag("/videos/video.webm") shows href="/videos/video.mp4".
  • picture_tag with several sources shows <source> elements without the type attribute. Each one gets a type from the file extension, as the existing tests in asset_tag_helper_test.rb expect.
  • video_tag(..., poster: "screenshot.png", poster_skip_pipeline: true) shows poster="screenshot.png". The poster goes through image_path with skip_pipeline: true, which returns /images/screenshot.png.
  • asset_path("application.js", skip_pipeline: true) and asset_path("filedoesnotexist.png", skip_pipeline: true) show paths without a leading slash. compute_asset_path joins them to the public directory, so they start with /, like the type: examples right below them.

Detail

This Pull Request changes the example output in those docs to match what the helpers render. No code changes.

Additional information

Output on main (ActionView::Base.empty, no asset pipeline):

preload_link_tag("/videos/video.webm")
# => <link rel="preload" href="/videos/video.webm" as="video" type="video/webm">
picture_tag("picture.webp", "picture.png")
# => <picture><source srcset="/images/picture.webp" type="image/webp" /><source srcset="/images/picture.png" type="image/png" /><img src="/images/picture.png" /></picture>
asset_path("application.js", skip_pipeline: true)
# => "/application.js"
asset_path("filedoesnotexist.png", skip_pipeline: true)
# => "/filedoesnotexist.png"

With compute_asset_path overridden to return /assets/... (as an asset pipeline gem does):

video_tag("trailer.m4v", size: "16x10", poster: "screenshot.png")
# => <video poster="/assets/screenshot.png" width="16" height="10" src="/assets/trailer.m4v"></video>
video_tag("trailer.m4v", size: "16x10", poster: "screenshot.png", poster_skip_pipeline: true)
# => <video poster="/images/screenshot.png" width="16" height="10" src="/assets/trailer.m4v"></video>
asset_path("application.js", skip_pipeline: true)
# => "/application.js"

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because some of the examples in the FormTagHelper API docs don't render what they show.

  • range_field_tag 'quantity', in: 1...10 passes the options hash as value (the signature is range_field_tag(name, value = nil, options = {})), so it renders value-in=""1...10"" instead of min="1" max="9". The min:/max:/step: example has the same problem, and its output is missing the closing />.
  • time_field_tag and datetime_field_tag document an :include_seconds option, with an example showing value="01:01:00.000". Only the FormHelper versions (time_field / datetime_field, through Tags::TimeField / Tags::DatetimeField) handle that option. The tag helpers pass it straight to text_field_tag, which renders it as an include_seconds attribute.

Detail

This Pull Request changes:

  • The two range_field_tag examples to pass nil as the value, like the number_field_tag examples already do, and adds the missing />.
  • The time_field_tag and datetime_field_tag docs to drop the :include_seconds option and its example.

Additional information

Output on main:

range_field_tag("quantity", in: 1...10)
# => <input type="range" name="quantity" id="quantity" value-in=""1...10"" />
range_field_tag("quantity", min: 1, max: 10, step: 2)
# => <input type="range" name="quantity" id="quantity" value-min="1" value-max="10" value-step="2" />
time_field_tag("time", "01:01", include_seconds: true)
# => <input type="time" name="time" id="time" value="01:01" include_seconds="true" />

With the examples in this change:

range_field_tag("quantity", nil, in: 1...10)
# => <input type="range" name="quantity" id="quantity" min="1" max="9" />
range_field_tag("quantity", nil, min: 1, max: 10, step: 2)
# => <input type="range" name="quantity" id="quantity" min="1" max="10" step="2" />

I didn't add :include_seconds support to the tag helpers, since that would be a behavior change rather than a docs fix.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because the :validate section of the Association Basics guide says the default is always false and that has_and_belongs_to_many does not support the option. Both are wrong, and a reader following the guide would expect a parent with an invalid new child to save when it doesn't.

Reflection#validate? returns options[:validate] when it's given, and otherwise options[:autosave] == true || collection?:

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7d52e0123842/activerecord/lib/active_record/reflection.rb#L741-L742

The API docs already describe this correctly (+true+ by default for has_many and has_and_belongs_to_many, +false+ by default for has_one and belongs_to), and has_and_belongs_to_many passes :validate through to the has_many it builds.

Detail

This Pull Request changes the :validate section to say that the default depends on the association type (true for has_many and has_and_belongs_to_many, false for belongs_to and has_one unless :autosave is true), and removes the paragraph saying has_and_belongs_to_many does not support the option.

Additional information

Checked on main with SQLite by building one invalid associated record and saving the parent:

Association save
has_many (default) false
has_many validate: false true
has_and_belongs_to_many (default) false
has_and_belongs_to_many validate: false true
has_one (default) true
has_one autosave: true false
belongs_to (default) true
belongs_to autosave: true false

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #58870.

ActiveSupport::IsolatedExecutionState.share_with copies the execution state hash but not the values inside it. ActionController::Live calls it so the streaming thread starts with the request's state. As a result, the request thread and the streaming thread push to and pop from the same connected_to stack array.

The request thread returns the response while the streaming thread is still running. When it then leaves a connected_to block, such as the one ActiveRecord::Middleware::ShardSelector opens around the whole request, the frame is also popped from the streaming thread's stack, so the rest of the stream runs on the default shard and role. The reverse also happens: while a connected_to block entered on the streaming thread is open, it changes the role and shard the request thread sees.

Detail

This Pull Request changes connected_to, connected_to_many and connecting_to so they no longer modify the stack in place. Pushing and popping build a modified copy and store it in the current execution state, which leaves the array the other thread holds untouched. prohibit_shard_swapping already treats its set this way (prev_value.dup.add(...)).

The stack is still a mutable array, so code that pushes or pops it directly (for example the connected_to_stack.pop calls in base_test.rb) keeps working.

Tests:

  • BasicsTest: after the parent thread leaves connected_to and connected_to_many blocks, a thread that shares its state still sees both roles. It got [false, false] before this change.
  • BasicsTest: a connected_to(role: :reading) block on a thread that shares the state no longer changes the parent's role. Before this change the parent's current_role was :reading.
  • ShardSelectorTest: a thread started inside the middleware keeps running after the middleware returns (as ActionController::Live does) and still sees shard_one. Before this change its current_shard was :default.

On the fork's CI (Ruby 3.4), bundle exec rake test:sqlite3 in activerecord reports 9851 runs, 35079 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 39 skips with this change. Without the library change, the only failures are the 3 new tests. test/controller/live_stream_test.rb (45 runs) and test/isolated_execution_state_test.rb (13 runs) pass, and RuboCop reports no offenses in the touched files.

Additional information

The other values in the execution state are still shared by reference. The issue raises the broader question of whether share_with should copy some keys deeply. This change leaves share_with alone and only fixes the stack Active Record uses to route queries, so the connection handler and the other shared objects keep their identity. config.action_controller.live_streaming_excluded_keys = [:active_record_connected_to_stack] still works as before.

Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because three reachable branches in ActionDispatch::PermissionsPolicy had no test coverage, while the matching branches in ContentSecurityPolicy are tested (test_missing_context_for_dynamic_source, test_raises_runtime_error_when_unexpected_source).

Line coverage from test/dispatch/ + test/controller/ showed these lines never ran:

  • apply_mapping: raise ArgumentError, "Unknown HTTP permissions policy source mapping: ..."
  • resolve_source: raise RuntimeError, "Missing context for the dynamic permissions policy source: ..."
  • Middleware#call: headers.delete(FEATURE_POLICY) when the policy has no directives

Detail

This Pull Request adds three tests, one per branch:

  • test_unknown_source_mapping: geolocation :non_existent raises ArgumentError
  • test_missing_context_for_dynamic_source: build with no context and a Proc source raises RuntimeError (mirrors the CSP test of the same name)
  • "empty policies will not set a header": the middleware leaves no Feature-Policy header for a policy with no directives

To support the third test, the middleware test's PolicyConfigMiddleware now takes the policy as an argument (default unchanged).

I mutation-tested each branch to confirm the tests actually catch breakage:

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Related to #58834.

Some PostgreSQL extensions create tables, enum types and even schemas of their own when they are installed. PostGIS creates spatial_ref_sys, pg_partman creates part_config and part_config_sub, the PostGIS tiger geocoder creates a few hundred tables, and Citus creates the enum types citus.distribution_type and citus.shard_transfer_mode along with the schemas citus, citus_internal, columnar and columnar_internal. PostgreSQL treats all of these as part of the extension: DROP EXTENSION removes them, and you cannot drop or recreate one of them on its own.

Today db/schema.rb lists these objects like any other. Tables and enum types appear as soon as their schema is on schema_search_path, and installing an extension into public, which is the default, is enough; schemas appear with dump_schemas = :all. The dump itself succeeds, but loading it does not: create_table ..., force: :cascade tries to drop a table that belongs to an extension, or a create_schema gets in the way of the extension script that expects to create that schema, and the load stops right there.

PG::DependentObjectsStillExist: ERROR:  cannot drop table part_config because extension pg_partman requires it
PG::ObjectNotInPrerequisiteState: ERROR:  schema columnar is not a member of extension "citus_columnar"

Applications on PostGIS usually do not notice, because activerecord-postgis-adapter has carried a hand-maintained list of PostGIS table names in ignore_tables since 2011. Everybody else has to discover the problem and maintain such a list themselves, or switch to structure.sql, which does not have the problem: pg_dump never writes out the objects an extension owns and leaves them to CREATE EXTENSION.

Detail

PostgreSQL records which objects belong to an extension in pg_depend, with deptype = 'e'. The dumper now asks for that list once and leaves those tables, enum types and schemas out of db/schema.rb. The enable_extension line already recreates them on load, exactly as CREATE EXTENSION does in structure.sql.

Nothing else changes. connection.tables and table_exists? still return these tables, and an object that an application attaches to an extension itself with ALTER EXTENSION ... ADD is left out as well, which is also how pg_dump treats it.

With PostGIS and pg_partman installed into public, the dump goes from this:

  enable_extension "pg_partman"
  enable_extension "postgis"

  create_table "part_config", primary_key: "parent_table", id: :text, force: :cascade do |t|
    ...
  end

  create_table "part_config_sub", primary_key: "sub_parent", id: :text, force: :cascade do |t|
    ...
  end

  create_table "posts", force: :cascade do |t|
    ...
  end

  create_table "spatial_ref_sys", primary_key: "srid", id: :integer, default: nil, force: :cascade do |t|
    ...
  end

to this, which loads into a fresh database:

  enable_extension "pg_partman"
  enable_extension "postgis"

  create_table "posts", force: :cascade do |t|
    ...
  end

Additional information

  • This Pull Request is related to one change. Changes that are unrelated should be opened in separate PRs.
  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: [Fix #issue-number]

  • CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #33155. The issue was long ago reported by many users, including us. We have been using our own internal patch, that worked for our CI, now we are extending it to include the other scenarios mentioned. @adrianna-chang-shopify and @matthewd offered on #54280 to run a new attempt against their apps' CI (originally authored by @joshuay03)

A new record's has_one :through and has_many :through readers return nil / [] even when the through records are already in memory:

comment = Comment.new(post: Post.new(author: author))
comment.author # => nil

doctor = Doctor.new
doctor.appointments.build(patient: patient)
doctor.patients # => []

#51114 (by @joshuay03) fixed this, with follow-ups #53869, #53957, #54046 and #54238, and all of it was reverted in #54280 (by @adrianna-chang-shopify). This is a second attempt that addresses both reasons for the revert:

  1. The previous code walked reflection.chain and called middle.association(reflection.source_reflection_name) at each step. That name belongs to the class one level up, not to the record being walked. Every chain shape needed its own fix (belongs_to middles, singular middles in collection chains, polymorphic reflections), and a source renamed in the middle of the chain still raised AssociationNotFoundError at the time of the revert.

  2. Autosave couldn't tell records assigned to the association (which need a join record on save) from records reached through join records that already exist. It built a second join record (#54176). The previous fix for that then skipped assigned records that did need one, which is the regression test added in the revert.

I asked an AI to generate an executable test case with every example from the above threads, plus guard tests for what caused the revert. It is at https://gist.github.com/sromano/3dc83cf160dc0f85d620983b513ee64d. The same gist has a per-test comparison of main, the reverted implementation and this branch.

through_new_records_test.rb pass fail
main 12 32
main before #54280 26 18
this branch 44 0

Detail

Reading (ThroughAssociation#target_from_through_records): only for a new owner without a foreign key to query by.

  • Walks through_reflection and then source_reflection recursively, using each record's own association. Nested associations, belongs_to middles, renamed sources and polymorphic sources need no special cases.
  • Uses what is in memory and loads what isn't. A persisted middle's through association is walked only when it's fully loaded, and queried otherwise.
  • source_type and STI class_name are filtered with is_a?(reflection.klass), like the type condition in the query. Through records that are destroyed or marked for destruction are skipped.
  • An association whose own scope filters records (where, joins, limit, …) is not inferred and returns nothing until save, as today. distinct is applied.
  • A middle record that would raise StrictLoadingViolationError is not lazily loaded.

Keeping reached records apart from assigned ones:

  • HasManyThroughAssociation tracks reached records separately and recomputes them on each load_target while the owner is new. size, empty?, include? and *_ids agree with to_a.
  • HasOneThroughAssociation flags an inferred target. It is recomputed on each read while the owner is new, and read from the database once the owner is saved.
  • Autosave neither validates nor saves reached records; their own parents do, exactly as before.
  • concat and replace keep working on assigned records only. patient_ids= on a new record doesn't drop join records built by hand, and assigning a reached record makes it an assigned one, as before.

Persisted owners are not affected.

Additional information

  • The reverted tests are restored, with the model associations they relied on. New tests cover renamed sources, source_type, reassigning a through record, distinct, filtering scopes, records marked for destruction, replace on a new record, and autosave not validating or duplicating reached records.
  • Cost, new owner with 100 in-memory join records: doctor.patients.to_a takes 139 µs, against 88 µs for doctor.appointments.map(&:patient) done by hand. comment.author takes 5.3 µs, against 2.0 µs for comment.post.author. << on a new owner is unchanged. Benchmark script in the gist.
  • Not addressed here (neither on current main): the join record described twice, e.g. doctor.patients.build plus doctor.appointments.build(patient: patient) (#54176 scenarios 2 and 3, and the second test of #54238). Those create two join records on Rails 7.2 and 8.0 too. The previous attempt only passed scenario 3 (and not 2 anyway) through #54238's filter, which is what broke #54280. They're in a separate script in the gist, duplicate_join_records_test.rb: all three fail on 7.2, 8.0, main and this branch. They would be better handled in a follow-up to save_through_record for someone interested in those scenarios.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

For validations using except_on:, errors.added? returns false even when the requested error is present. errors.details also includes the validation's except_on callback option.

class Post
  include ActiveModel::Model
  attr_accessor :title
  validates :title, presence: true, except_on: :draft
end

post = Post.new
post.valid?                        # => false
post.errors[:title]                # => ["can't be blank"]
post.errors.added?(:title, :blank)  # => false, expected true
post.errors.details
# => { title: [{ error: :blank, except_on: :draft }] }
# Expected: { title: [{ error: :blank }] }

Detail

Add :except_on to ActiveModel::Error::CALLBACKS_OPTIONS, alongside :on. This makes the existing filtering logic treat it consistently with the other validation callback options.

Extend the error matching and details tests, plus the validation integration test. The integration test also checks that validation remains skipped in the excluded context and leaves no errors.

Additional information

The option was introduced in #43495. Reproduced against upstream main at 7601afd65c748f8354b947d55c75b77b35c5b50b using Ruby 3.4.7.

Related issue #54483 and fix #56546 addressed callback options supplied in the lookup: options were filtered from the stored error but not from the query. This patch addresses a distinct omission in the recognized callback-option list; the lookup above passes no callback options at all. Searches across open and closed issues and PRs found no report of this specific except_on matching/details failure.

  • Before the fix: the three regression checks fail for the incorrect matching and details.
  • After the fix: 3 runs, 8 assertions, no failures, errors, or skips.
  • Full Active Model suite: 1,226 runs, 5,448 assertions, no failures, errors, or skips (cd activemodel && PARALLEL_WORKERS=1 bin/test).
  • RuboCop passes for all three changed Ruby files.

  • This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why.
  • Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
  • CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #58865.

With config.active_record.encryption.extend_queries = true, a deterministic encrypted attribute that also declares normalizes silently stops matching rows stored unencrypted (support_unencrypted_data: true) or with a previous scheme's key. The extended uniqueness validation also stops detecting duplicates on case-sensitive collations.

Detail

normalizes wraps the attribute's EncryptedAttributeType in a NormalizedValueType, whose serialize casts before delegating. The extended query support passes previous-scheme values through as AdditionalValues, and only EncryptedAttributeType knew to serialize them as-is. The wrapper instead string-cast the AdditionalValue, normalized it and encrypted the result, so the query's IN (...) contained a value that could never match.

This Pull Request changes:

  • NormalizedValueType#cast now returns an AdditionalValue unchanged when extended queries are installed, so it reaches the encrypted type's existing passthrough.
  • The queried value is cast (and therefore normalized) before previous-scheme values are built, consistent with the value queried under the current scheme.
  • ExtendedDeterministicUniquenessValidator passes the previous-scheme ciphertext as an AdditionalValue, so the normalizer is no longer applied to the ciphertext.

Additional information

I hooked cast rather than serialize on purpose. Prepending serialize onto NormalizedValueType makes serialize_cast_value_compatible? return false, which makes records normalize their values twice when saved (caught by NormalizedAttributeTest#test_minimizes_number_of_times_normalization_is_applied).

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Newly generated tests all use tmp/generators as the destination_root. prepare_destination deletes and recreates the destination_root before each test runs. Multiple tests running in parallel will delete each other's destination_root, causing flaky tests. Two different tests that create the same file in the same directory will also sometimes fail.

Detail

This Pull Request uses a temporary directory for each test to isolate the test run and avoids collisions. Deleting the destination_root can no longer happen in setup because we will no longer have access to the name. It must be handled in teardown.

Additional information

This change is extracted from changes to RubyEvents generator tests - rubyevents/rubyevents#1934
We started off with the default template and ran into quite a few issues before landing on this one.

items.content_html:
This PR is part of the Rails Foundation documentation project and updates the Autoloading and Reloading guide. The new guide is now open for community review (and it has been reviewed by the author of Zeitwerk, @fxn).

The changes are mainly focused on enhancing the content of the existing guide with further elaboration, spelling things out a bit more and adding examples.

Add Introduction and motivation for autoloading - how constants work in Ruby and why require is needed

Add explanation for how autoloading works

Explain the high level difference between autoloading, eager loading, and reloading up front

Explicitly state the difference between 'main' and 'once' autoloader

Move Eager loading and Reloading further up, as understanding reloading is needed for other sections

Add a note about zeitwerk_enabled? to the Engines section, as it might be most relevant there

Add a code example for autoload_lib_once

Eager loading section: elaborate on what eager_load_all does in the last paragraph. Elaborate on what's the consequence of saying it's "COW-friendly" in the first paragraph.

Reloading section: elaborate that reloading does not "update" an object but rather unloads and then autoloads again. Add the consequence and solution for the "stale object" situation.

Autoloading Without Reloading (autoload_once_paths) section: Explain the MyDecoration example a bit more

New section:

Expanded the last section (Rails.autoloaders) into a new section - How Zeitwerk Interfaces with Rails (inspeired by the [fxn comment](https://3.basecamp.com/3076981/buckets/35498807/todos/9183284516#__recording_10017040619) on the basecamp task).
items.title: Update Autoloading and Reloading Rails Guide

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

has_one_attached and has_many_attached accept only dependent, service, strict_loading, and analyze, so their generated ActiveStorage::Attachment associations cannot receive other association options such as validate:, deprecated:, collection callbacks like after_add:, or options added by application and gem extensions. The current workaround is to redeclare the association, duplicating its internal scope, class_name, as:, inverse_of:, and dependent: :destroy settings and relying on Active Storage internals.

Detail

Both macros now accept **options and pass them only to the attachment association, not the blob through association. The options come last so they can override Active Storage’s defaults. This mirrors delegated_type forwarding extra options to belongs_to. Unknown options still raise, through has_one or has_many option validation rather than the macro’s keyword arguments.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Combining a callable value_method with a selected or disabled Proc raises TypeError in collection select helpers. Both options are supported individually. For example, a collection_select with computed option values and a predicate that disables unavailable records fails while rendering the form.

This also reproduces directly with:

options_from_collection_for_select(
  [1, 2],
  ->(number) { number },
  :to_s,
  ->(number) { number == 2 }
)

The second option should be selected. Instead, extract_values_from_collection passes the value Proc to public_send and raises TypeError.

Detail

Use the existing value_for_collection helper when extracting selected and disabled values, matching the way option values are rendered. This supports callable values while preserving public_send behavior for method names.

Add regressions for callable values combined with selected and disabled Procs, plus a collection_select example that verifies computed values, model selection, and disabled options together.

Additional information

Reproduced against rails/rails main at 2cc9c08699bc8062c0851dab772cbea64affabda using Ruby 3.4.7.

  • Before the fix: all three new tests raise the expected TypeError.
  • After the fix: all three pass.
  • Full Action View suite: 3,285 tests, 7,437 assertions, no failures, errors, or skips (cd actionview && PARALLEL_WORKERS=1 bin/test).
  • RuboCop passes for both changed Ruby files.

Searched open and closed Rails issues and PRs for the helper, value methods, and Proc selection/disabled combinations; found no matching report. Related PR #57163 documents callable value/text methods but does not address this combination.

Checklist

  • This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why.
  • Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
  • CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries.
items.title: Fix callable collection values with selection and disabled Procs

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because SecureRandom.base32 (added in #56288) is meant for one-time codes that people read and type by hand, but its alphabet still contains 0 and 1. Crockford's Base32 handles 0/O and 1/I/L confusion at decode time by treating the lookalikes as equal. Rails only generates these codes and doesn't provide a decoder, so apps usually compare them as exact strings. A user who types O for 0 (or I/L for 1) gets rejected unless each app adds its own normalization.

Detail

This Pull Request changes SecureRandom.base32 to SecureRandom.base30, which also leaves out 0 and 1. The alphabet is now 23456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ. None of 0, O, 1, I or L can appear, so codes can't be misread, even in typefaces where those characters look alike, and no decoding rules are needed.

SecureRandom.base30     # => "FYWCJTEVA78KM8C3"
SecureRandom.base30(24) # => "SVE9HA8Q3SXE5AVB63JMNVGS"

base32 hasn't been released yet (it's only on main, planned for 8.2), so this renames it instead of deprecating it. The CHANGELOG entry and the 8.2 release notes are updated to match.

Additional information

Each character now carries log2(30) ≈ 4.91 bits instead of 5, so a 16-character code has about 78.5 bits of entropy instead of 80. For short human-entered codes, avoiding misreads seems worth that small cost.

cc @monorkin @miharekar, the authors of #56288.

Checklist

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

When a tracked variant is first processed, Active Storage currently publishes its variant record before uploading the image. A failed upload leaves a record that marks the variant as processed, preventing regeneration. Concurrent requests can also observe the record before its image is available.

Related to #55088.

Detail

This change does not alter when variant processing starts: lazily processed variants are still generated on first use. Once processing begins—whether lazily, immediately, or in a background job—upload the image before creating or finding its variant record. The record therefore remains an availability marker for a successfully uploaded variant.

Delete uploaded files on transaction rollback, and defer enqueuing purge jobs for failed or unused blobs until the enclosing transaction commits.

Add regression tests for upload visibility, retry after failure, rollback cleanup, record creation failures, and deferred purging. A concurrency test uses two threads with separate SQLite connections and synchronization barriers to verify that both callers resolve to the same variant record and only the losing upload is purged.

Additional information

Validation on Ruby 4.0.5:

  • Full Active Storage suite: 618 tests, 1919 assertions, no failures or errors.
  • Four MuPDF tests skipped because mutool is unavailable.
  • S3/GCS service tests were not enabled because credentials were unavailable.
  • JavaScript lint/build consistency check passed.
  • RuboCop passed for both changed Ruby files.
  • git diff --check passed.
  • The concurrency regression test fails against the implementation before this fix.

Checklist

  • This PR contains one related change.
  • The commit explains what changed and why, with a related issue reference.
  • Regression tests are included.
  • The Active Storage changelog is updated.
items.title: Upload tracked variants before publishing records

items.content_html:
Stacked on #58844, #58845, #58846 and #58847. This is the top of the stack;
its diff is the final commit only.

Motivation / Background

Migration version compatibility has an adapter-specific side: what
Migration[6.1] does with :datetime depends on whether the adapter is
PostgreSQL, what Migration[5.1] does with create_table depends on whether
it is MySQL, and so on. Today ActiveRecord::Migration::Compatibility decides
this with connection.adapter_name string checks inside the version classes.

That has two consequences:

  • A third-party adapter cannot take part except by patching the version
    classes.
  • An adapter that subclasses a bundled one, such as one reporting
    "CockroachDB" on top of PostgreSQL, never matches the string check, even
    though it uses the parent's schema statements.

Supersedes #58162, which was split into #58844, #58845, #58846, #58847 and
this PR.

Detail

The adapter now owns its part of the compatibility.

  • A connection adapter resolves a migration's declared version to a
    CompatibilityBehavior class through a new compatibility_behavior_for
    hook, and Migration#method_missing runs every schema operation through an
    instance of it.
  • A behavior class covers its own version and older. Its methods adjust the
    arguments and call super, the same idiom the version classes use. Nested
    TableDefinition modules handle t.<something> calls inside blocks.
  • An adapter that does not implement the hook gets a base behavior that does
    nothing, so it behaves exactly as before.

The PostgreSQL and MySQL adjustments move into PostgreSQL::CompatibilityBehavior
and MySQL::CompatibilityBehavior. No adapter_name checks remain in
compatibility.rb. SQLite3 has nothing adapter-specific left after #58845, so
it defines no behaviors. The explicit proper_table_name call that #58846
added to V5_1#change_column is no longer needed, because behaviors receive
table names with the prefix and suffix already applied.

Two things worth knowing when reading the diff:

  • V5_0 injects default: nil for integer primary keys. MySQL must keep auto
    increment on a bigint primary key, so the injected value carries a marker
    that lets the MySQL behavior drop it without touching a default: nil the
    migration wrote itself.
  • The verbose message is now built where the operation executes, so it shows
    the options as a behavior actually runs them. Table names are still printed
    as written in the migration.

Additional information

Migrations on the bundled adapters produce the same schema and the same
verbose output as before. The DDL for the affected operations was captured for
every version from 4.2 to current on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL, and it is
identical before and after this change.

Checklist

  • This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: [Fix #issue-number]
  • Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
  • CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Additions to CHANGELOG files should be in the same format as the existing entries. See the guidelines for writing CHANGELOG entries.
items.title: Move adapter-specific migration compatibility into per-adapter behaviors

items.content_html:
Stacked on #58846.

Motivation / Background

Several migration compatibility version classes carry a TableDefinition
module that adjusts t.<something> calls inside create_table and
change_table blocks. To activate it, each of those classes (V8_0, V7_0,
V6_1, V6_0, V5_2, V5_0 and V4_2) repeats the same private method:

def compatible_table_definition(t)
  t.singleton_class.prepend(TableDefinition)
  super
end

The method has no content of its own. It exists only so that the chain of
super calls prepends every module on the way up, and every new version class
with a module has to copy it.

Detail

Replaces the seven copies with a single implementation in
Migration::Current#compatible_table_definition. It walks the migration's
ancestors, and for every version class that defines a TableDefinition
module, prepends that module. A version class now only declares its module.

The walk goes oldest version first, so the newest version's module ends up
first in method lookup. That is the same order the chained super calls
produced, so method resolution inside the blocks does not change.

No behavior change. The migration compatibility tests exercise these modules
across versions and pass unchanged.

Additional information

The copies accumulated one version class at a time: 214dc7d (V5_0 and
V4_2), #34970 (V5_2), #38717 (V6_0), #41084 (V6_1), #43904 (V7_0) and
#55086 (V8_0).

Checklist

  • This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: [Fix #issue-number]
